Tropones with Zwitterionic Allenyl Palladium Species Derived from

ABSTRACT: A palladium-catalyzed regioselective [8 + 3] cycloaddition of tropsulfimides and tropones with vinyl-
idenecyclopropane-diesters (VDCP-diesters) has been disclosed in this paper, affording decahydro-1H-cyclohepta[b]pyridine
derivatives bearing an allene moiety or decahydro-1H-cyclohepta[b]pyran derivatives having a conjugated diene unit in moderate to
good yields. The reactions proceed through a zwitterionic allenyl palladium species derived from VDCP-diesters. The substrate
scopes have been investigated and the plausible reaction mechanisms have also been proposed according to the previous work, the
first captured zwitterionic Pd-allenyl intermediate, and control experiments.
■
INTRODUCTION
Allenes, recognized as cumulated dienes, and conjugated
dienes have been widely used as useful building blocks in
natural product synthesis,
1−3
medicinal chemistry,
4
and
material science
5−7
as well as fine chemical synthesis.
8−15
Particularly, substances containing allene and conjugated diene
subunits have drawn significant attention from organic
chemists for the preparation of complex molecular skeletons.
16
Among their synthetic methodologies, the allenyl or propargyl
palladium species derived from an oxidative addition of
propargyl derivatives bearing a leaving group plays a key role
for the rapid preparation of various allene and conjugated
diene derivatives (Scheme 1a).
17−23
In general, as for these
propargyl derivatives having the large alkyl or aryl substituents
located at the leaving group site, the allenic product can be the
major one if in the presence of a bidentate phosphine ligand
upon nucleophilic addition (Scheme 1a).
24−26
However, when
the substituents at the leaving group site are two hydrogen
atoms or small alkyl or aryl groups, the conjugated diene can
become the major product in the presence of a monodentate
phosphine ligand (Scheme 1).
27
The production of an alkynyl
compound from nucleophilic substitution of allenyl or
propargyl palladium species is relatively rare (Scheme 1).
Sometimes, adjusting the nucleophilicity of the employed
nucleophile can alter the distribution of allenes and conjugated
dienes.
28−31
On the other hand, the zwitterionic allenyl or propargyl
palladium species, as a special type of allenyl or propargyl
palladium species, has been seldom seen in organic synthesis
although its analogues such as zwitterionic π-allyl palladium
species have been widely used in palladium-catalyzed chemical
transformations (Scheme 1b).
32−45
In this aspect, zwitterionic
allenyl or propargyl copper species generated from acetylenyl
ethylene carbonates or carbamates
46−48
have been used in the
nucleophilic substitutions for the production of alkynyl or
allenyl derivatives (Scheme 1b).
49−51
In 2021, our group reported the first example on the
generation of zwitterionic allenyl or propargyl palladium
species from vinylidenecyclopropane-diesters (VDCP-die-

First, the substrate scope for the production of 3 was
examined and the results are shown in Scheme 2. A wide range
of tropsulfimides 1 reacted with the zwitterionic allenyl
palladium species generated from VDCP-diesters 2 smoothly,
affording the desired cyclized products 3 in moderate to good
yields. Regardless of whether an electron-withdrawing or
-donating substituent was introduced at the para-position of
the benzene ring linked to sulfimides, the target products 3a−
3j were obtained in 63 to 91% yields, suggesting that the
electronic property of these substituents did not have
significant impact on the reaction outcome. The substituent
at the meta-position of the benzene ring also gave the
corresponding cycloadducts 3k−3m in 47 to 88% yields. It
should be noted that introducing a methyl group at the ortho-
position of the benzene ring delivered 3n in 74% yield;
however, introducing a bromine atom at the ortho-position did
not afford 3o, presumably due to the steric effect.

Tropsulfimides 1p and 1q having a heterocycle or a fused
aromatic ring were also tolerated, giving the desired products
3p and 3q in 89 and 67% yields, respectively. A sterically bulky
aromatic ring such as a mesitylene group probably impaired
the cycloaddition reaction and did not give the corresponding
product 3r under identical conditions. Meanwhile, introducing
a variety of alkyl groups to sulfimides 1 afforded the
corresponding products 3s−3v in moderate to good yields
ranging from 68−96%. In the case of sulfimide 1w, the desired
cycloadduct 3w was obtained in 32% yield probably due to the
steric effect as well. However, using sulfimide 1x as a substrate,
in which a strongly electron-withdrawing CF
3
group was
introduced, did not furnish the cyclized product 3x perhaps
due to the electronic effect leading to the weak N-
nucleophilicity of sulfimide 1x.
Furthermore, a variety of VDCP-diesters were compatible to
this reaction, affording the desired [8 + 3] cycloaddition
products 3y−3ab in good to excellent yields ranging from 72−
92%. However, the reactions did not proceed smoothly when
the terminal position of the allene moiety in 2 was changed
from the ethyl to a phenyl group or an isopropyl group was
added on the cyclopropane ring. The corresponding products
3ac and 3ad were not formed under the standard conditions.
Remarkably, substrate 1ae containing a malononitrile moiety
instead of a sulfimide unit, which was prepared upon
condensation between tropone and malononitrile, underwent
a [6 + 3] cycloaddition reaction pathway rather than a [8 + 3]
cycloaddition process probably due to the steric effect,
furnishing the corresponding product 3ae in 82% yield. Its
structure has been clarified by X-ray diffraction, and the related
CIF data are depicted in the Supporting Information.
Next, the substrate scope for the production of 5 using
tropones as substrates was subsequently explored and the
results are exhibited in Scheme 3. A variety of tropones 4 were
employed to react with VDCP-diesters 2, providing the
products 5 in moderate to good yields. Introducing various
substituents at the para-position of the benzene ring located at
the 2-position of the cycloheptatriene ring furnished the
corresponding products 5a−5h in the yields of 41−80%, also
rendering that the electronic property of these substituents did
not have significant impact on the reaction outcome. In
addition, tropone 4i bearing a cyano group at the meta-position
of the benzene ring gave the desired product 5i in 48% yield.
Introducing a chlorine atom at the ortho-position of the
benzene ring such as tropone 4j did not give the desired
product 5j perhaps due to the steric effect. Moreover, tropones
4k and 4l containing a fused aromatic ring and a heterocycle
could also be tolerated, furnishing the corresponding products
5k and 5l in 63 and 48% yields, respectively. Nevertheless,
tropone 4m only with a methyl group and tropone 4n without
any substituent could not react with 2a to give the
corresponding cycloadducts, presumably due to their low
reactivity with the zwitterionic allenyl palladium species
generated from VDCP-diesters. Meanwhile, changing the
ester group in VDCP-diester 2 from the ethyl group to an
isopropyl group or benzyl group smoothly delivered the
corresponding cycloadducts 5o and 5p in 63 and 72% yields,
respectively. The other electron-withdrawing groups such as
OTs or Cl located at the 2-position of the cycloheptatriene
ring were also tolerated, giving the desired products 5q and 5r
in the yields of 74 and 78%, respectively. Tropones 4s and 4t,
derived from hinokitiol, a natural product, also had excellent

To illustrate the practicability of these reactions in organic
synthesis, a large-scale synthesis of 3a or 5e was performed by
using 1a (259 mg, 1.0 mmol) or 4e (0.210 g, 1.0 mmol) to
react with 2a (0.35 mL, 2.0 mmol) under the standard
conditions, affording 3a or 5e in 42 or 48% yield, respectively
(Scheme 4). The discrepancy between a template reaction and
a large-scale synthesis is presumably due to the different
thermal, anaerobic and heterogeneous experimental condi-
tions. Likewise, the catalytic asymmetric version of this
cycloaddition was also investigated (see Scheme S4 in the
Supporting Information for more details), and we found that
the use of chiral phosphine ligands L15 and L16 delivered 3a
in 13 and 15% yields, respectively, along with −40 and 35% ee
values (Scheme 4b). The slight discrepancy is probably due to
the experimental error or the partial decomposition of 3a
during the reaction. On the other hand, we have also tried the
synergistic catalysis by adding a chiral ammonium salt as
reported previously;

obtained (see Scheme S4 in the Supporting Information).

(MALDI-MS), providing the first experimental evidence on

suggesting that the zwitterionic palladium species might be
derived from the oxidative addition of the palladium catalyst
with the cyclopropane ring in VDCP-diesters (Scheme 5c).
To further understand the substrate-induced selectivity,
density functional theory (DFT) calculations of the rearrange-
ment part were performed (Figure 1). All calculations have
been performed at the SMD(THF)/B3LYP-D3BJ/ma-
def2TZVP/SDD//B3LYP-D3BJ/6-31G(d,p)/SDD level with
the Gaussian 16 program. An evident difference was shown
between the dissociation of tropsulfimide and tropone that the
former was an exothermic process to form the product and
regenerate the key intermediate int-1, while the latter was an
endothermic process to form product-o. Moreover, the
rearrangement of the allenyl product as int-V to the conjugated
diene product as 2a was exothermic, relatively elucidating the
substrate-induced selectivity of the reaction.
On the basis of the above experimental results and the
previously reported processes, plausible mechanisms for the [8
+ 3] cycloaddition of tropsulfimides and tropone derivatives
with zwitterionic allenyl palladium species, which can also
isomerize to a zwitterionic propargyl palladium species, are
proposed in Scheme 6. A coordination between the
palladium(0) complex and VDCP-diester 2a formed complex
I and induced an oxidative addition to take place at the
electron-deficient C−C site of the cyclopropyl unit to form
intermediate II that can isomerize to zwitterionic propargyl
palladium species II′, which underwent the cycloaddition
reaction with tropsulfimide 1 or tropone derivative 4 to afford
intermediate III. Since then, intermediate IV was generated via
a chair-form X

■
CONCLUSIONS
In summary, a novel and regioselective [8 + 3] cycloaddition of
tropsulfimides and tropone derivatives with zwitterionic
palladium intermediates generated from VDCP-diesters has
been realized, providing decahydro-1H-cyclohepta[b]pyridine
derivatives bearing an allene unit or decahydro-1H-cyclohepta-
[b]pyran derivatives containing a conjugated diene moiety in
moderate to good yields depending on the C = X (X = N or
O) bond in tropone derivatives. Their substrate scopes have
been investigated, and the key zwitterionic palladium
intermediate was verified through MALDI mass spectroscopy
for the first time. The plausible reaction mechanisms have been
proposed. Further investigations on the synthesis of bio-
logically active cycloheptatriene derivatives are undergoing in
our laboratory.
■
